  "reasons": [
    "The scenario in the stem is taken directly from NCERT Class 12 Business Studies Chapter 1, which uses a petrol pump, a hospital, a school, and managers in India, Germany, and Japan to illustrate that management is all pervasive."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Nature & Significance of Management",
  "syllabus_topic": "Management – concept, objectives, importance",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "The scenario describes managerial activities being common across different types of enterprises (petrol pump, hospital, school) and different countries (India, Germany, Japan).",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "strongest_reading": "The stem mentions carrying out managerial activities, but does not describe the temporal continuity or simultaneous performance of planning, organising, directing, staffing, and controlling.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "strongest_reading": "The stem describes individual leaders across three unrelated entities, not diverse individuals within one organization coordinating their team efforts.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "The stem highlights that managerial activities are universally performed across sectors and countries, not that specific organizational goals are being united.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "blocking_defects": [],
  "style_notes": [],
  "cuet_fit": {
    "criteria": {
      "syllabus_objective": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Directly tests identification of features of management, a core Class 12 Business Studies objective."
      },
      "format_authenticity": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Standard single-stem conceptual case application MCQ matching CUET UG Business Studies items."
      },
      "level_calibration": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Aligned with typical CUET UG comprehension and application items from NCERT textbook scenarios."
      },
      "discrimination_value": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "All four options feature genuine characteristics of management from NCERT, testing conceptual differentiation."
      }
    },
    "reasoning_steps": 1,
    "estimated_difficulty": "easy",
    "cognitive_level": "comprehension",
    "exemplar_ids_compared": [
      "cuet2024-business_studies-bookA-q41",
      "cuet2024-business_studies-bookA-q44",
      "cuet2024-business_studies-bookA-q45"
    ]
  },
  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Management is a continuous process, because functions are performed by all managers all the time",
      "premise_source": "case_scope",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "A petrol pump owner in India, a hospital administrator in Germany and a school principal in Japan all carry out the same managerial activities, although the way they do them differs because of culture, tradition and history.",
      "reason": "The stem describes cross-sector and cross-national universality, not the continuous temporal cycle of management functions."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Management is a group activity, because it needs team work and coordination of individual effort",
      "premise_source": "case_scope",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "A petrol pump owner in India, a hospital administrator in Germany and a school principal in Japan all carry out the same managerial activities, although the way they do them differs because of culture, tradition and history.",
      "reason": "The case describes individual administrators in separate institutions, not team work and coordination within an organisation."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Management is a goal-oriented process, because the efforts of individuals are united towards organisational goals",
      "premise_source": "case_scope",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "A petrol pump owner in India, a hospital administrator in Germany and a school principal in Japan all carry out the same managerial activities, although the way they do them differs because of culture, tradition and history.",
      "reason": "The case does not focus on uniting individual efforts toward an organisational goal."
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "(ii) Management is all pervasive: The activities involved in managing an enterprise are common to all organisations whether economic, social or political.",
      "reason": "NCERT explicitly links the petrol pump, hospital, school, and cross-national examples to pervasiveness."
    }
  ]
}
